summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins support front-end work and design ideation by mining ~810 past sessions from the orin-dx-site and pages projects, then use the findings to simplify the plugins toward an agentic, low-ceremony v5 (core, courier, muse, mason, plus a wisp-packs plugin).
summary.outcome: Four investigations confirmed the plugins were too rigid for exploratory work and could not capture visual intent. The v4.6.0 release shipped with PR #23 merged, 11 plugin tags and a GitHub release. Wisp-packs ideas were saved to memory, six parallel v5 tracks were launched, and a release-script resume fix was committed on a new branch.

repo: Only 2 real sessions exist in the orin-dx project dir and ~7 in pages; the ~700 other jsonl files are subagent transcripts, so session counts are misleading.
Plugin agents appeared in only two top-level sessions across the corpus; design ideation ran through Artifacts, forks, general-purpose agents and local dev servers with screenshots.
Plugin spend was about 23% and ad hoc forks/general-purpose agents about 77%; value came from first-round independent checks against code or a build, while later gate rounds were waste.
spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints, visual references or motion, so a spec can pass the binding exit-gate while saying nothing about appearance.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that doesn't exist (introduced in commit a859e2f), so implemented accessibility is never checked.

The release process has three levels: shipped (merged with version bump), pinned (tags vX.Y.Z and <plugin>--vA.B.C) and announced (GitHub release); scripts/release.py originally treated a locally existing tag as 'already exists' and could not resume a partial push.
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is substituted in skill and agent text, while relative shared/ paths cause failed first reads.
Gate outputs are enforced by shared/hooks/validate-handback.py (RETRY_CAP=1) and routing by shared/hooks/route-guard.py, which uses atomically created per-fact files to be race-free.
plugin.json is the single source of truth; tools/sync-claude-manifests.py generates marketplace entries, README version lines and Codex manifests.
In pages, repo-wide pre-commit gates cost many waits during parallel smith runs, and large 60-130KB spec/plan files stalled agent streams.

code.finding: Release tool now edited so a locally existing but unpushed tag is pushed instead of refused, letting a partial tag push resume; covered by updated tests/test_release.py and committed on a new branch.
RETRY_CAP = 1: a fail on the second round must carry an escalation_required blocker, and any later report must be an escalated fail.

workflow: Subagent reports are model output without user authority; mechanical transcript scans plus parallel analysis agents worked well for large-corpus evaluation.
For ideation, rendered options the user can pick from (boards, screenshots) work far better than text descriptions; the user repeatedly had to ask 'show me'.
Parallelize with separate worktrees and files, using Opus for core builds and Sonnet for well-specified edits.
Don't write code during design discussions; the user stopped this explicitly.
Avoid human ceremony: default reversible decisions, reserve the owner's attention for PR approvals, credentials, taste calls and facts only they know.
Don't bypass merge queue or required review (no --admin); don't work around the pr-bot token failure, use Entire trails to open PRs.

Sandbox and guard quirks: use plain commands, /usr/bin/git and the Write tool for scripts; GPG signing, network and cross-repo writes need sandbox override; transient GitHub push errors succeed on retry.
Always verify subagent output for invented content (e.g. a fabricated 'Revisit when' line in ADR 007).

friction: Orchestrator ignored the gate's escalate signal (carried on with an 'owner-directed gate pass') and the 3-retry cap, causing long gate loops in pages.
Specs were not judgeable by the user without pictures; visual defects (nav sheet not full screen, translucency, touch targets) were caught only by the user's eye after gates passed.
Design decisions were lost across sessions ('did you lose that decision. I'm frustrated').
Guard refusals on compound git commands, heredocs and $(...) forced command rewrites.
Sandbox blocks and transient GitHub push errors (including one v4.6.0 tag rejection) required retries and manual release creation.
PR creation was blocked because gh couldn't mint an orin-dx-pr-bot token, and PR #23 was blocked by required review and the merge queue.
Early answer that 4.6.0 was 'not properly released' overstated the situation and needed correction.
Backstory ablation was first scored wrongly because the scorer read tool results and matched fixture text, and the ablation setup had background-agent and deleted-diff bugs.
The user was frustrated when I began writing probe code during a design discussion and when I implied I'd run the release.
open_items: ADR review of 011 (presented) and 012-017 one at a time; ADR 014 needs a real read since it partly reverses ADR 009. The user later said re-reviewing was ceremony, so this is likely superseded.

Integrate the six parallel v5 tracks (wisp core, wisp-packs, delete eight old plugins, remove Codex/Antigravity machinery, tidy, project repo cleanups) onto one v5-core branch and dogfood in the four repos.

Build wisp-packs v0: markdown packs, /packs:load, /packs:list, /packs:suggest and session-start hook; mine rust-house and ts-house; unverified slash-command argument handling; catalog location and naming undecided.
Later wisp CLI (wisp suggest, packs show/vendor) as a deterministic engine.
Resolve the three Entire findings on trail #386.
Brand source of truth (orin-dx-site/brand vs Pages) blocks the UI pack; status of orin-dx-site unclear.
Caliper's hard-coded rustup path and Pages' rtk rule cleanups.
Delete merged remote branches and stale worktrees; the release-script fix is committed on a branch but not yet PR'd or merged.
Nothing yet measured on whether the changes reduce gate rounds, turns or tokens; the TokenEconomizer trial needs approval since it writes settings.
Plugin gaps found by the evaluation: no sketch/spike mode, no visual or browser capability, no decision log, no promote-prototype-to-spec path, and the muse a11y taxonomy doc defect.
